title: Severe drowsiness and hypercapnia on the medical ward
summary: A 71-year-old woman with severe COPD and chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure is found unrousable with high oxygen flow.
rationale: Elderly female with chronic CO2 retention and compensatory metabolic alkalosis (baseline standard bicarbonate 34 mmol/L) presenting with acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure and hyperoxaemia (SpO2 95% on 4 L/min nasal prongs). Re-tests SpO2 target selection (88-92%), ABG compensation recognition, and timely NIV initiation. Engine note: the engine models a modest FiO2-dependent rise in V/Q dead space in chronic retainers, so oxygen alone nudges PaCO2 up; headless at 30 sim-min with no other treatment, 4 L/min gives PaCO2 82 mmHg / pH 7.24 / SpO2 91% vs 1 L/min giving PaCO2 80 mmHg / pH 7.25 / SpO2 82%. The CO2 difference is small (about 2 mmHg) because the dead-space effect is modest and hypoxaemia on 1 L/min adds fatigue, so the lesson is a controlled target (88-92%, about 2 L/min gives SpO2 87% at 30 min) plus early NIV, not withholding oxygen.

retestsMistake.clinicalFocus: SpO2 target selection (target 88-92% rather than hyperoxaemia) in acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure (high FiO2 modestly worsens CO2 retention; hypoxaemia is also harmful)

source: O'Driscoll BR, et al. BTS guideline for oxygen use in adults. Thorax 2017;72 Suppl 1:ii1-90; Rochwerg B, et al. ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines. Eur Respir J 2017;50:1602426; teaching-convention

changes.vignette: Female 71, chronic baseline bicarbonate 34 mmol/L, found drowsy on 4 L/min nasal prongs.

sex.reason: Female patient with smaller baseline tidal volumes

ageYears.reason: Elderly cohort typical for advanced home COPD

patient.presentingStory: Admitted yesterday with acute infective exacerbation of COPD. The overnight nurse calls because she is somnolent, flapping tremor present, and oxygen was turned up to 4 L/min two hours ago when her saturations dipped to 86%. She is currently on nasal cannula 4 L/min with SpO2 97%.
patient.history: Severe COPD (FEV1 32% predicted, chronic retainer with baseline PaCO2 56 mmHg), osteoporosis. Dependent on mobility frame. No formal DNAR or treatment limitations.

findings.examine: Markedly somnolent, rousable only to loud voice. RR 26, shallow breathing, prominent coarse expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Coarse asterixis on hand extension. Warm, bounding pulse.
findings.cxr: Marked hyperinflation, flattened hemidiaphragms, widened intercostal spaces. No focal consolidation or pneumothorax.
